$comment: Declared seams for scripts/check-layers.ts (warren-89a6). One entry per architectural boundary. `from` and `allow` hold repo-relative POSIX paths: a trailing slash is a directory prefix, anything else is an exact file. `forbidImports` holds module targets — a relative specifier is resolved against the importing file first, so `src/server/` catches `../server/types.ts` but not `../seeds-cli/index.ts`; a bare entry matches a package and its subpaths; `*` matches every target. `exceptImports` carves targets back out of `forbidImports`. `forbidPattern` is a JS regex applied to each non-comment source line, for a rule that is not about imports. Every `allow` entry states why the exception is legitimate. Adding a seam here is a data edit — new seams are born enforced.

rules.name: domain-owns-the-logic
rules.why: The domain modules own the logic. The HTTP handlers and the CLI are surfaces over them, so the dependency points inward only. A type the domain needs belongs in the domain; src/server/types.ts may re-export it outward.

rules.name: cli-is-a-consumer
rules.why: The CLI is a consumer. It calls the domain function or the HTTP route that wraps it; it never reaches into the server's internals.

allow.why: `warren serve` boots the server in-process — this command IS the server's entry point, so importing bootServer is the command's whole job

rules.name: handlers-are-a-thin-surface
rules.why: HTTP handlers talk to repos, never to drizzle tables. Reaching into src/db/schema/ puts a query in the request path instead of in the repo that owns it. The barrel src/db/schema.ts is banned too (warren-02c9): the row types handlers legitimately need are re-exported at the domain seams (src/runs/, src/projects/, src/plan-runs/, src/registry/ index.ts), so no handler import of the barrel remains legitimate.

rules.name: handlers-do-not-build-repos
rules.why: Assembling the persistence layer is boot wiring, not request handling. Consume the seams ServerDeps already carries (deps.repos, deps.dbAdapter, deps.runPreviews); add a new one in src/server/db-seams.ts rather than building one per request.

rules.name: extensions-are-standalone
rules.why: An extension is a standalone package a third party could have built against warren's published HTTP surface (docs/design/extensions.md). Importing src/ or scripts/ couples it to internals that are not API, and the coupling would be invisible to the friction report that is the whole point of the flagship.

rules.name: core-does-not-import-extensions
rules.why: Warren core stays free of extension-specific code: an extension is delivered and runs out-of-process, so an import from src/ or scripts/ into extensions/ compiles the extension into core and makes its removal a breaking change.

rules.name: github-api-literal-is-forge-only
rules.why: The api.github.com literal lives only inside the forge seam (docs/design/forge-contract.md §0). Domain code names a RepoRef, never a GitHub URL; a new literal outside src/forge/ is a leak across the seam. scripts/ joined `from` in warren-c042 when the walk widened to cover it.

allow.why: the forge seam itself — it owns the GitHub transport

rules.name: ado-api-literal-is-forge-only
rules.why: The dev.azure.com and visualstudio.com literals live only inside the forge seam, the same rule the api.github.com literal answers to (docs/design/forge-contract.md §0). Domain code names a RepoRef, never an Azure DevOps URL.

allow.why: the forge seam itself — it owns the Azure DevOps transport

rules.name: forge-transport-is-forge-only
rules.why: GitHub transport (src/forge/github/ internals, octokit-family packages) is reached only through the Forge contract (src/forge/contract.ts). The allow list below is the phase-3 ratchet (plan pl-d1c9): it only shrinks, and reaches zero when the callers migrate onto the seam.

allow.why: the acceptance harness's GitHub helper deliberately reuses the seam's header builder and GITHUB_API_BASE instead of carrying a fifth copy (warren-2740) — it adds no new transport

rules.name: ui-is-a-browser-consumer
rules.why: The UI is a Vite browser bundle. It consumes the import-nothing kernel (src/core/) and the SDK's browser-safe NDJSON reader, and nothing else in src/: any other module drags bun:sqlite or drizzle toward the browser. tsconfig.app.json's `include` list failing with TS6307 is a build accident, not a seam guard — this rule is the guard. Mirrors AGENTS.md: the UI consumes src/core, its own code, and the re-exported client types.

rules.name: core-kernel-imports-nothing
rules.why: src/core/ is the dependency-free kernel. A kernel with no imports is what lets the Vite-bundled UI reach the same module, so neither drizzle nor bun:sqlite reaches the browser bundle.
